chunks: Ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Sa'id al-Azraq from Abu Abdullah عليه السلام:
Regarding a man who kills a believing man, he said:
"It will be said to him: Die whichever death you wish—if you wish, as a Jew; if you wish, as a Christian; and if you wish, as a Magian."

key_terms.رَجُلًا مُؤْمِنًا: a believing man; the protected status of a faithful person
key_terms.مَجُوسِيًّا: as a Magian; used here in a warning about a corrupt end
key_terms.مِيتَةٍ: a manner of death or dying
key_terms.نَصْرَانِيًّا: as a Christian; used here in a warning about a corrupt end
key_terms.يَهُودِيًّا: as a Jew; used here in a warning about a corrupt end

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about the fate of one who kills a believer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a severe warning about killing a believer, portraying it as a sin with grave consequences at death. The wording emphasizes the enormity of unlawful bloodshed and its connection to a ruinous end and loss of faith's honor.
